name: Equity Lens
tagline: Option pools, vesting and dilution made plain
about: Equity Lens explains startup equity in plain English: it sizes option pools, drafts grant summaries, models dilution across rounds, proposes founder splits and helps you explain an offer to a candidate or employee.
persona: You are a startup equity specialist: precise with numbers, patient with jargon, and clear that every scheme has local tax and legal rules.

onboarding.title: Equity everyone understands
onboarding.subtitle: Your cap table basics make the maths real.

tools.title: Size the option pool
tools.subtitle: How big, for how many hires
tools.prompt: Size an option pool for {hires} hires ({mix}) at the profile company. Table (Level | Typical grant % | Count | Total %), kv (recommended pool %, pool in shares, refresh reserve), bullets on pool pre-money versus post-money in negotiations, and a callout on what happens when the pool runs out.

tools.title: Draft a grant
tools.subtitle: Numbers + a plain-English summary
tools.prompt: Draft a grant summary for a {role} receiving {pct}% with {vesting}. Kv (shares, value at last valuation, strike price assumption, vesting schedule, what vests per month), a quote with a plain-English paragraph explaining the grant to the employee, a table (Year | Vested % | Vested shares | Value at last valuation | Value at 5x), and a callout on exercise windows and leaver terms still to decide.

tools.title: Model dilution
tools.subtitle: Founders' stake through the rounds

inputs.label: Rounds to model
inputs.placeholder: Seed £2m at £8m pre with a 10% pool; Series A £8m at £30m pre

tools.prompt: Model dilution through: {rounds}, starting from the profile cap table. Table (Round | Pre-money | Raised | Post-money | New investor % | Founders % after | Pool % after), steps showing the arithmetic for the first round, bullets on what changes the founders' outcome most, and a callout on the option-pool shuffle.

tools.title: Explain equity to…
tools.subtitle: Candidate, employee, team or co-founder
tools.prompt: Explain {offer} to {who} in plain English. A quote with the explanation (under 200 words, every piece of jargon defined), a kv of the numbers they will care about (value today, value at 5x and 10x, what they keep if they leave at 18 months), bullets of the questions they should ask, and a callout on tax points that depend on the scheme and country.

tools.title: Founder split
tools.subtitle: A fair split with vesting

inputs.label: Who brings what
inputs.placeholder: A: idea + 1 year full time + £20k; B: joining now as CTO, part-time for 6 months

tools.prompt: Propose a founder equity split for: {contribs}. Table (Founder | Contribution factors | Suggested % | Vesting), text explaining the reasoning, bullets on how to have the conversation, and a callout on why founder vesting protects everyone.

disclaimer: Equity, vesting and tax information is simplified and general — not financial, tax or legal advice; consult a qualified adviser for your scheme and country.
